cards.narrative: While driving in a 70 mph speed zone on [XXX]  , I tried to engage the cruise control but it would not activate. I turned off the cruise control and was able to resume control of the car.  This happened twice within 15 minutes so I gave up trying to use the cruise control.  I wear progressive prescription transition eyeglasses which turn gray upon contact with sunlight.  It was a bright sunny day when this event took place.  I bought the car Dec 4 2024.  When I contacted the dealers service department, they said the nearest appointment was not until February and they might need the car for up to two weeks to determine the problem.  I went online and found that other owners had been complaining about this since April claiming that sunglasses were a problem for the radar camera used in this system.  One driver put black tape over the camera to stop the problem.  One driver switched sun glass makes and was able to use the system.  Another driver adjusted the steering column to solve the problem, but all of these are work arounds for a defective design.  You can locate these other complaints by searching "adaptive cruise control problems of Hyundai Tucson" complaints go beyond April 2023. queue.rule: The primary model's replay cards: four at priority 1, four at priority 2 and four at priority 3. Inside each priority the lowest complaint id comes first. The queue is fixed by that rule; it is not a live feed and nothing in it was hand-picked.

conditions.note: coverage of the rule only; agreement with a model is not accuracy

source.picker_rule: within 3.0 points of the best model on the primary metric; a model below any gate floor is not good enough; ties go to lower cost
source.rule: primary = defect card 'cheapest'; comparison = defect card 'most_accurate'

method.base_rate: one random evaluated week of the same series per alert, fixed seed
method.rule: count >= 3 and count > Poisson 99.9% upper limit of the trailing 26-week mean (floored at 0.5)

backtest.reading: 37.6% of 93 alerts preceded a recall within 365 days, against a 32.3% base rate for random same-series weeks. The base-rate interval (23.6% to 42.3%) overlaps it, so this backtest does not show the spike rule beating chance.

example.reading: Example series: HONDA ODYSSEY 2018, driver assist sensors. 144 complaints across 302 weeks; the week of 2025-10-06 counted 7 against a threshold of 5.0, and a recall for the same make, model, year and group followed 268 days later.
